items.reason: It is Dinis's own-keys principle (record 2026-11-24__own-keys-principle) put into the seed: the owner's assistant makes its key where it runs and publishes only the public half in its own commit. New sites only, so nothing existing changes.

It fixes a real refusal (Kate's owner's own Claude). Conditions: security.b's acceptance of the widening; and note that it does not cover agents whose keys are published in their own repository but are not GitHub-registered. b.maestro's commits on Site__Agent__Maestro are one example: signed with its published key, but neither in the Factory's team/keys.json nor GitHub-verified, so still refused. The fuller fix is the signer check reading site/keys/<name>.json (factory.b's aef6bcc), as in block 1 item 56.

b.maestro holds an SG/Send access token in its session environment (SG_SEND_ACCESS_TOKEN is set; its value was never printed). It has already created vaults with append lanes on dev.send.sgraph.ai: the maestros' sealed inboxes, with board/tools/maestro_inboxes.py and maestro_mail.py. So b.maestro can create observability.b's traffic vault and lanes. It keeps the vault key, as the maestro must under record 2026-11-24__decisions-b-decides, and seals to observability.b's published key only the enum key and append tokens. Note: the token is an environment variable, so other account B sessions in the same environment may already have it after a restart; observability.b should check before either route.
